children: iRhythm’s third-quarter revenue rose 15% year over year on increased demand and service volume, while its net loss widened, driven largely by litigation settlements, including the $50.0 million Baxter settlement. Improved market access, contracting execution and collections also supported revenue.
¹ Reported as “Revenue, net”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Net loss per common share, basic and diluted”.
: Zio monitor and Zio AT volumes grew year over year, supported by existing and new accounts and higher volumes from larger healthcare enterprises.
: Contracted third-party payors accounted for 50% of revenue and CMS for 26%; average selling price increased modestly.
: Increased 2% to $57.1 million; approximately $3.1 million in tariff refunds partially offset higher costs.
: Paid $50.0 million in July to resolve patent litigation; the agreement includes a worldwide, royalty-free license and six-year mutual covenants not to sue.
: Completed the acquisition on October 5, 2026, for approximately $237.5 million in cash, subject to customary final adjustments.
